goal: Carry the boundary's decision audit onto the one path a real Python ASGI host actually drives. P21C made every authorization decision durably auditable, P21D carried that audit to the ASGI callable and P21E closed the identity-guard silence — but host/js_asgi/create_customer_asgi_runner.mjs, the process the Python StdioJsAsgiBridge spawns per request, still composed the unaudited createCustomerAsgiComposition, so a request that arrives the way it will really arrive committed with no decision on record. This package adds exactly one additive, explicit, value-bearing --audit on|off runner argument whose default is off. Only an explicit --audit on, and only together with an explicit --policy allow, selects createAuditedCustomerAsgiComposition; the host then supplies the two collaborators that composition deliberately does not own — a dependency-free canonical Crockford-base32 ULID generator whose 48-bit millisecond prefix is this process's own clock reading and whose 80 random bits come from node:crypto, and a real UTC-millisecond instant. Neither the id nor the instant can be injected through a CLI argument. An omitted --audit and an explicit --audit off are the same runner: the no-args default, --policy deny and unaudited --policy allow compose exactly what they composed before. The fixed expectations stay owned by the frozen test file; this manifest describes the scenarios, binds the provenance and gates the run, and supplies no expected value back to any assertion.

Nothing about hashing, chaining, evaluation or persistence is reimplemented here, and no new module, dependency, framework or host was introduced — the ULID and the instant are twenty lines of Node standard library, not a package.

No test was weakened, skipped or made conditional; the frozen test was never edited and its sha256 is unchanged from the handoff snapshot. The --audit value is mandatory and closed: a missing value, a following flag read as a value, an unknown value and a case-shifted value are each a deterministic non-zero exit with an empty stdout, taken before stdin is read and before any database is contacted, and --audit on outside --policy allow is refused the same way. The audit is opt-in and is never switched on behind the caller. A decision that cannot be recorded propagates out of app and the process exits non-zero with nothing on stdout, so an unrecordable decision can never answer an unaudited 2xx at the host boundary.

auditedHostRunnerContract.substrate: one migrated real PostgreSQL 16 container, driven only through the real Python StdioJsAsgiBridge into separate JS runner processes, shared by P21F-1 through P21F-4 within a single test
auditedHostRunnerContract.explicitValueBearingArgument: --audit takes exactly the value on or off. A bare --audit with no value at all, a --audit whose value is the next flag, an unknown value and a case-shifted value are each a fail-closed malformed-CLI-args exit that names the exact malformed input, writes no ASGI response event and contacts no database.
auditedHostRunnerContract.defaultOff: an omitted --audit and an explicit --audit off are the same runner. The no-args default, --policy deny, --policy deny --audit off, --audit off with no --policy, and an unaudited --policy allow all compose createCustomerAsgiComposition from exactly the collaborators they composed it from at this base.
auditedHostRunnerContract.allowOnly: --audit on is admissible only together with --policy allow, because deny mode never reaches a database and so has no decision worth a durable record; turning the audit explicitly off there is not an error. Neither --audit value relaxes allow mode's existing --connection-string, --trusted-tenant-id and --trusted-actor-id requirements: each refusal still arrives deterministically, before any composition and before any database contact.
auditedHostRunnerContract.hostSuppliedCollaborators: the audited composition mints no id and reads no clock of its own, so the host process supplies both, from the Node standard library alone — no ULID package, no date library, no dependency change. The ULID is canonical Crockford base32, twenty-six uppercase characters, ten of them this reading of the clock as a 48-bit big-endian millisecond count and sixteen of them the low five bits of sixteen node:crypto bytes, exactly uniform because 256 is a whole multiple of 32. The instant is the same process's own reading in the canonical UTC millisecond form the Clock port admits. Neither may be named by a CLI argument: a host that let a caller supply the id or the time of its own audit row would be recording the caller's claim rather than what happened.
auditedHostRunnerContract.identityUnchanged: the audited allow takes its authenticated identity from the same two trusted CLI inputs of this process and from nothing else. The request's own x-tenant-id / x-actor-id headers stay claims the composition compares, so a claimed foreign tenant or actor keeps its exact existing 403 and its refusal is filed under the trusted identity, never the claimed one.
auditedHostRunnerContract.failClosed: with the decision log's INSERT grant revoked on the live substrate the append refuses, the refusal propagates out of app, the runner process exits non-zero with nothing on stdout, and the Python bridge answers its own 502 subprocess_failed. No 2xx, no CommitReceipt, no business row and no decision row appears.
auditedHostRunnerContract.provingMethod: whole-database count(*) over each write table as the superuser, with no tenant filter and no row-level predicate, so no write can hide behind a scope; and every column of every row of all four tables projected to text through to_jsonb and searched for each attacker-claimed value, so a claimed tenant or actor cannot survive anywhere the test never thought to read.
auditedHostRunnerContract.expectedValuesOwnedBy: the frozen test file only: the argument spelling, every refusal message, status, outcome, error code, decision payload fields, chain linkage, ULID and instant forms and the bracket arithmetic are all asserted there and are never read back out of this manifest.
auditedHostRunnerContract.manifestRole: the manifest is a load-bearing gate: the frozen test refuses to run any P21F scenario unless this file exists and declares exactly the five scenario ids in order.

The audit is opt-in by construction. A host that forgets --audit on gets the unaudited runner and no warning, because making it default-on would change the existing default path this package is required to preserve. Making the audit mandatory is a later, separate decision.
